checks: The submission expressly calls itself a response to the government bill and its summary says changes to the government draft are needed. The investment sentence names section24; it is not presented as a quotation of the July consultation draft.

The September operative provision requires global diversification and delegates asset classes. Its memorandum favours a high equity share but does not establish an exclusive statutory equity obligation.

The earlier July operative text affirmatively contains the claimed exclusive rule, giving a particularly strong benign carry-over explanation. This explains rather than eliminates the mismatch against the version expressly addressed.
The October committee text later adds the equity-only rule; it must not be used to rescue a22September submission. The side-by-side official text independently corroborates the original gap.

Minor is appropriate because the request additionally concerns broad market diversification, passivity and costs, none of which follows from equity-only allocation. The claim does not invalidate the overall reform position.
direction_assessment: False is defensible only for the general request to bind more investment requirements in the statute: the mistaken claim understates existing discretion and correcting it strengthens the case for statutory specification. It has no demonstrated direction for whether a particular portfolio or passive strategy is preferable. Null would be more conservative if direction were confined to the separate passivity/cost demands, but the explicit overarching request supports the narrow false assessment.
adjudication: Retain minor/false exact-version description, with earlier-draft explanation and limited policy implications prominent. No claim of intentional misdescription or eventual investment outcome.
